verdict.rationale: Mem0 documents its own expiration_date on a memory: once the date passes, the memory stops surfacing in search but is not deleted. That gives a manually set 'invalid-after' timestamp separating current from expired facts. Nothing shows facts carrying valid-from times, automatic invalidation of superseded facts, or querying what was true at a past time. Missing for 10: valid-from/valid-to tracking on facts or graph edges, automatic invalidation when contradicting facts arrive, point-in-time temporal queries, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can track when facts became valid or invalid (temporal reasoning) so the memory distinguishes current from outdated information

citations.quote: Set an expiration_date on a memory and Mem0 stops surfacing it once that date passes
Set an expiration date on a Mem0 memory and it stops surfacing in search once that date passes. Nothing is deleted. Works on Platform and Open Source.
